messages:
oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] ALERT 2624000001 — StratusBank (dedicated pool: sb-eu-west-1) p99 latency spike > 15s. Pager: leo (oncall). Impact: user-facing timeouts on payments. War room: https://redwood/warrooms/2624000001 :rotating_light:
leo (oncall): i'm looking. creating thread for mitigation coordination. pinging SREs + runtime.
leo (oncall): quick context: StratusBank runs in their dedicated VPC/pool (sb-eu-west-1). we have recent runtime deploy at 02:12 UTC (kernel selection heuristics).
samir (SRE): grabbing prometheus. query: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le,cluster,pool))` -> sb-eu-west-1 p99 = 17.8s, p95 = 3.4s, overall error rate + 1.6% 5xx.
samir (SRE): trend looks like sharp increase starting 02:24 UTC. correlates w/ `runtime/opt-kernel-v2` rollout to sb pool.
ella (eng-runtime): noted. I rolled opt-kernel-v2 to a subset of dedicated pools at 02:15 for performance gains; sb-eu-west-1 was in the canary. no alerts during internal testing tho.
aisha (AM): customer is actively seeing payment timeouts. they just messaged account slack: "we're seeing errors in payments, can you confirm?" — they're escalation-ready.
netty (infra): checking node-level metrics. CPU on GPU hosts is normal, but host-level iowait on two nodes in pool is high (0.6s). diskio wait + NVMe telemetry shows spikes.
samir (SRE): can we try isolating the pool from the kernel change? rollback or pin to opt-kernel-v1?
ella (eng-runtime): two options: 1) rollback runtime rollout for that pool (safer), or 2) temporarily route StratusBank traffic to warm spare pool in eu-west-3. rollback will require a rolling restart of serving pods (will cause short reconnects).
leo (oncall): priority = reduce customer impact asap. i prefer traffic move to warm spare while we validate rollback.
opsbot: runbook lookup -> "dedicated-pool-high-latency" recommended actions: `isolate-tenant`, `drain-and-cordon`, `route-weights` change.
jamie (support): i'll draft a short note to customer: "We're investigating elevated latency. We've initiated mitigations and will follow up in 15 min with status."
samir (SRE): start mitigation: isolate noisy tenant processes and shift traffic. commands: ```
# isolate tenant traffic to warm spare
rwctl pool route set --from=sb-eu-west-1 --to=sb-eu-west-3 --weight=1.0 --customer=stratusbank
# cordon & drain problematic hosts
kubectl cordon gpu-node-34 -n redwood-serving
kubectl drain gpu-node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-serving
```
netty (infra): i've flagged gpu-node-34 and gpu-node-37 as tainted (taint: redwood=tainted:NoSchedule). running maintenance job to evict pods now.
ella (eng-runtime): also disabling the opt-kernel-v2 flag for sb pool config to stop further kernel selection for new sessions: `redwood-config set pool.sb-eu-west-1.runtime.kernel=opt-kernel-v1` then `svc rollout restart pool/sb-eu-west-1`. doing that now.
samir (SRE): monitoring p99 after route shift — give it ~30s to settle 
(00:35 UTC) samir (SRE): p99 dropped to 2.1s, p95 0.9s, errors trending down. partial relief observed.
leo (oncall): good. continue to keep traffic on eu-west-3 warm spare while we confirm stability.
aisha (AM): communicating to StratusBank: short note -> "We've routed your traffic to a warm spare region (eu-west-3) to restore performance. We're investigating root cause and will share next steps. No action needed on your side." (sent) :white_check_mark:
jamie (support): customer confirms partial recovery on their side, fewer timeouts reported.
ella (eng-runtime): rolling restart completed for sb-eu-west-1 with kernel pinned to opt-kernel-v1. however some sessions are closed — expected.
opsbot: incident timeline entry created: mitigation step: route-shift -> eu-west-3 at 00:34 UTC.
samir (SRE): run quick perf regression to ensure no latent issue in warm spare: `ab -n 1000 -c 20 https://sb-eu-west-3.redwood/predict` -> p99 ~ 0.85s.
netty (infra): NVMe telemetry on the two tainted hosts shows queued IO ops reduced after eviction, but firmware traces show a long running GC on nvme-controller-2. we'll keep hosts out of rotation until maintenance.
leo (oncall): next steps: keep traffic on eu-west-3 for 60m, validate no regressions, then plan controlled migration back once sb-eu-west-1 is fully healthy. open follow-ups: postmortem owner, customer comms, infra maintenance window.
aisha (AM): customer wants ETA for full return to eu-west-1. propose 90m tentative — we'll confirm once infra remediation complete.
ella (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: opt-kernel-v2 chose a kernel path that regressed for certain sequence-length + batch-size combos interacting with host NVMe GC behavior. postmortem pending.
samir (SRE): adding temporary alert: high-p99 + nvme-iowait correlation for dedicated pools.
leo (oncall): handing off to samir for night coverage. samir, you're primary for containment/validation. I'll update incident channel and remove myself after 15m.
samir (SRE): got it. i'll maintain and coordinate with infra to remediate nodes, and prepare postmortem draft.
jamie (support): drafting public-facing status page entry: "Degradation affecting StratusBank payments. We have routed traffic to warm spare and performance is restored. Investigating underlying cause." will post in 10.
opsbot: incident severity lowered from P0 -> P1 based on customer impact & mitigation.
samir (SRE): (01:30 UTC) p99 stable ~0.9s on eu-west-3 for 45m. nvme hosts in eu-west-1 out of rotation. starting root cause trace and reproducibility tests in staging for opt-kernel-v2.
leo (oncall): leaving war room. handing to samir. thanks team. :pray:
samir (SRE): final note before lock: postmortem owner: @ella (eng-runtime). communicate to customer: @aisha (AM). remediation: @netty (infra). follow-ups: schedule kernel rollout canary review and add NVMe health gating to rollout job.
jamie (support): closing warroom thread; will reopen if regressions.
on-visible-bot: archived war room 2624000001 after 80m.
__notes: This document is a single slack-thread representation. Messages are in chronological order in the 'messages' string. No title field per agents.md.
